cli.help.enc:
Usage:
  enc <input> [output] [options]

Arguments:
  <input>               File to encrypt (required)
  [output]              Defaults to "<input>.cbx"

Options:
  -p, --password <pass>  Passphrase on the command line (not recommended: stays in shell history)
  -a, --alg <id>         Cipher id, default 1 (AES-256-GCM)
  -k, --kdf <id>         KDF id, default 1 (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256)
      --iter <n>         Iteration count, default 600000
  -s, --strength <lvl>   Preset: quick / standard / strong (same as setting iterations)
      --chunk <bytes>    Chunk size, default 1048576 (1 MiB)
      --list             List available algorithms
  -f, --force            Allow overwriting an existing output file (refused by default)
      --display-name <n> Name to record inside the file (defaults to the real file name)
      --no-type-check    Mark the file to skip extension checks on any machine
      --compat-v1        Write a header identical to 1.3 and earlier (plain name, no category)
      --full-encryption  Encrypt the file name and hide the type (stored as "other")
  -v, --version          Show version
  -h, --help             Show this help

Examples:
  enc report.docx
  enc report.docx report.cbx -a 1
cli.help.dec:
Usage:
  dec <encrypted> [output-folder] [options]

Arguments:
  <encrypted>           .cbx file to decrypt (required)
  [output-folder]       Defaults to the folder of the encrypted file

Options:
  -p, --password <pass>  Passphrase on the command line (not recommended)
      --name <name>      Output file name (defaults to the name recorded in the header)
      --info             Show header information only, do not decrypt
      --view [bytes]     Read-only view without writing plaintext (default 65536 bytes)
  -v, --version          Show version
  -h, --help             Show this help

Examples:
  dec report.docx.cbx
  dec report.docx.cbx D:\out --name restored.docx
  dec report.docx.cbx --info
  dec notes.txt.cbx --view
  dec notes.txt.cbx --view 4096

conflict.heading: A file with the same name already exists
conflict.explain: Overwrite: replace the existing file with the archived content; the old file cannot be recovered. Skip: keep the existing file and do not extract this entry. Stop: abort the whole extraction; files already written stay on disk.
conflict.applyall: Use this choice for every later conflict
folder.hint.archive: Pack into one file: the whole folder goes into a single .cbx. Extraction is all-or-nothing; you cannot pull out one file separately. Good for handing a set of files to someone.
folder.hint.batch: Batch (one folder): every file is encrypted into its own .cbx inside a folder of the same name. Each file can be decrypted on its own; the batch shares one batch ID and decryption checks the whole set first. Good for archiving files you may need individually later.
